title: Open Forum Infectious Diseases — bacterial meningitis case (S. pneumoniae serotype 35B); CSF Gram stain and organism epidemiology

claims.text: S. pneumoniae cells are elongated ('lancet-shaped') cocci with a polysaccharide capsule, predominantly arranged in pairs (diplococci).
claims.byte_quote: Cells of _S pneumoniae_ are elongated ("lancet-shaped") cocci that are surrounded by a polysaccharide capsule and predominantly organized in pairs (diplococci).

claims.text: Other Gram-positive organisms causing meningitis in neonates and infants include Streptococcus agalactiae (Group B Streptococcus), a coccus in pairs and chains, and Listeria monocytogenes, a short rod.
claims.byte_quote: Other Gram-positive organisms that cause meningitis in neonates and infants include _Streptococcus agalactiae_ (Group B _Streptococcus_), a coccus ordered in pairs and chains, and _Listeria monocytogenes_, a short rod.

claims.text: Serotype 35B was the fourth most common invasive pneumococcal isolate (8%) among US children under 5 years of age in 2012–2013.
claims.byte_quote: serotype 35B was the fourth most common invasive isolate (8%) among United States children under 5 years of age in 2012–2013

claims.text: Serotype 35B became the most common penicillin-nonsusceptible serotype (24.8%).
claims.byte_quote: serotype 35B had become the most common penicillin-nonsusceptible serotype (24.8%)

claims.text: The patient's cytospin-prepared CSF Gram stain showed Gram-positive cocci in pairs, some within leukocytes, with a clear 'halo' around the intraleukocytic organisms (suggesting an encapsulated species).
claims.byte_quote: Gram-positive cocci arranged in pairs, some of which were within leukocytes

claims.text: A clear area ('halo') around the intraleukocytic organisms suggested an encapsulated bacterial species.
claims.byte_quote: A clear area ("halo") was apparent around the intraleukocytic organisms
